static_traits.name: Li Zhiyuan
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar problems in the past; not yet received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to identify and describe own negative Automatic thoughts; calm tone, Positive attitude, capable of self-Reflection

basic_info.main_problem: I often label myself a 'terrible Chef'; when things in the kitchen do not go as planned, I feel a sense of inadequacy. This thinking pattern started after I recently burnt a batch of brownies.
basic_info.core_demands: I notice these negative thinking patterns are affecting my self-esteem and my enjoyment of cooking (cooking used to be a source of joy for me), therefore I decided to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough/not good enough (when it comes to cooking)

special_situations.event: Burned the brownies while baking once
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail at a dessert, it proves I am a terrible cook
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces or avoids baking, with urges to give up cooking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible; I am not suited for cooking

special_situations.event: When dishes fall short of Anticipation or the finished product is not perfect enough
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the result is not perfect, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strictly copies tutorials, repeatedly consults recipes and tutorials to avoid any mistake

special_situations.event: Feels society's expectations and evaluation pressure regarding cooking performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot meet external standards and expectations, it means I am not good enough, I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling practice (watching tutorials, reading recipes), trying to do it with others or take classes to seek recognition
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Without others' approval, I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When reviewing cooking experiences, focuses more on failures and ignores successes (despite once making an apple pie everyone liked)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once I have failed, successes should not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly recalls failure experiences; lowers the weight given to positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I mess up often, which shows I am really not good enough

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and appreciated in cooking, and to maintain a sense of self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fear that failure or imperfection will lead to being negated, losing self-esteem and sense of worth
defense_goal: Through self-criticism/labeling, gains a sense of control and preemptively prevents further frustration
Reduces the risk of failure by avoiding or rigidly following rules

object_relations.self_representation: A failure easily negated (in the cooking domain)
object_relations.object_representation: Social others with high expectations and harsh evaluations

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing society's expectations of cooking, or when exploring external standards and evaluations in counseling
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe worth requires meeting external standards (treating others' values as unconditional self-standards)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use 'should/must' type statements for self-Demands, in a self-blaming tone, emphasizing external standards and others' eyes.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When dishes go wrong or the finished product is not perfect enough
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Divides self and outcomes into 'either perfect or terrible', finding it hard to integrate coexisting good and bad
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use extreme words (like 'always' 'never'), answering in negating language, with a Depression tone, ignoring middle possibilities.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited by the counselor to attend to success experiences or positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to deny or downplay positive evidence, maintaining a Self-denial narrative
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplays the significance of successful experiences, quickly turns back to failure details, with a dismissive tone, avoiding discussion of the impact of positive outcomes.

manifestations: Baking no longer brings joy the way it used to
Negative thinking reduces the experiential value of cooking
outcomes: Disruptions to daily routine and interests

manifestations: Feels pressure from society's expectations and evaluations of cooking
Hard to try and experience cooking at one's own pace and in one's own way
outcomes: Avoiding or rigidly following external standards

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should/must' type self-Demands to define good vs bad cooking
Treating social expectations as inviolable judgment criteria

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overly focuses on errors and mistakes, ignoring successful experiences
Blaming myself, thinking 'it is all because I am not good enough'

exception_events.target_problem: When mistakes happen in baking or cooking, Li Zhiyuan usually labels herself a 'terrible Chef', with Low mood and urges to give up
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once made an apple pie everyone loved and got positive feedback, different from the usual Self-denial narrative
exception_events.reason: Clues: the task and recipe were more familiar, focus was better, and mindset was calmer; thus on that occasion they experienced a more positive outcome and recognition from others

positive_force: Has had successful experiences (apple pie liked by others)
Willing to cook with friends and record the experience (open attitude toward behavioral experiments)
Having a good friend to talk with
Overall positive attitude, willing to change
negative_force: Self-harshness under the pressure of social expectations
Lowered Self-efficacy, with avoidance and giving-up tendencies

target_behavior.behavior: Self-denial after cooking/baking failures with urges to Avoids cooking (emotions: frustration, Anxiety)
antecedent: Errors occurring during baking or cooking (such as brownies being burnt)
Finished product falling short of Anticipation or not perfect enough
Thinking about society's expectations and judgments of cooking
target_behavior.core_reason: Generalizing one failure into overall incompetence, with Introjection of external standards, rigidly binding self-worth to outcomes
target_behavior.function: Escaping further failure and shame, protecting self-esteem and a sense of control in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence, Low mood, diminished enjoyment of baking and disrupted daily rhythms
